# devtrim

> Safe macOS developer-machine disk hygiene CLI & TUI (`v0.17.0`): measure, classify, and trim caches, stale build artifacts, `node_modules`, Xcode DerivedData/DeviceSupport, simulators, Docker/Buildx caches, Swift toolchains, installers, and agent caches — preview-by-default, Trash-first for filesystem targets, identity-verified, and write-ahead journaled.

- Website: https://mneves75.github.io/devtrim/
- Full Manual: https://mneves75.github.io/devtrim/MANUAL.html
- Source & Security Model: https://github.com/mneves75/devtrim
- Install (macOS arm64): `brew install mneves75/devtrim/devtrim`

## Rules for AI Agents

1. **Always preview first with `--json`.** Every `--json` invocation prints one JSON document to stdout and returns exit `0` on clean success, `1` on partial/scan/apply/runtime errors (including an unknown `optimize --task`), or `2` on invalid CLI flags or capability-scoped flag refusal.
2. **Never invent flags.** Mutation flags (`--apply`, `-y`, `--yolo`, `--shred`) are rejected with exit `2` on report-only commands (`worktrees`, `clean leftovers`, `app-storage`, `icloud`, `largest`, `explain`, `disk`, `history`, `status`, `analyze`, `dashboard`, `uninstall`).
3. **Prefer Trash-first for filesystem cleanup.** Default filesystem cleanup (`clean caches`, `purge`, `clean xcode`, `clean toolchains`, `clean installers`, `clean agents`) moves targets to macOS Trash (reversible). Only pass `--shred`, run `trash-empty --apply`, or run permanent command-based cleanups (`clean docker`, `clean simulators`) when the human explicitly authorizes permanent removal.
4. **Understand invocation boundaries.** Within a single invocation, apply consumes only that invocation's scanned plan (never rescans after confirmation), rechecks device/inode identity and build/Xcode/Docker liveness, and journals every attempt write-ahead to `~/.local/state/devtrim/journal.jsonl`. However:
   - A **separate** `--apply -y` (skips y/N prompts for danger ≤ 8) or `--apply --yolo` (also skips typed confirmation for danger ≥ 9) CLI invocation scans fresh — an earlier `--json` preview does not pin or constrain a later CLI process.
   - For `clean docker`, apply binds the previewed prune command and local endpoint (plus verified builder/nodes for Buildx), while Docker/BuildKit itself selects eligible unused images or cache records at execution time.
   - For `trash-empty`, `--confirm=<gb>` computes the integer by dividing the sum of **actionable** bytes from the new scan by `1 GiB` (`1024^3`) and truncating (flooring) to an integer, then accepts `±2` around that value.
5. **Respect what devtrim protects.** Docker volumes, Xcode Archives, Git repositories/worktrees, active builds, and `~/.ollama/models` / `~/.lmstudio/models` are never auto-deleted. Project cleanups (`purge`, `clean node-modules`, `clean artifacts`) skip directories holding Git-tracked files, and `clean artifacts` / `purge` additionally skip directories holding a Solana program keypair (`*-keypair.json`).

## Recommended Agent Workflows

### 1. Check free space (fast, read-only, exit 0)
```bash
devtrim disk --json
devtrim disk --warn-below 20GiB
```

### 2. Full read-only disk inventory
```bash
devtrim scan --json
devtrim worktrees --json
devtrim clean leftovers --json
devtrim largest --top 20 --json
devtrim explain /path/to/target --json
```

### 3. Safe Trash-first filesystem cleanup
```bash
# Preview current targets
devtrim clean caches --json
devtrim purge --json

# Non-TTY apply with actionable findings requires -y (danger <= 8) or --yolo (danger >= 9); empty plans skip confirmation.
# Note: this is a fresh scan and skips interactive confirmation; targets move to macOS Trash (reversible).
devtrim clean caches --apply -y --json
devtrim purge --apply --yolo --json
```

### 4. Reclaim disk space from Trash (only items devtrim moved; permanent)
```bash
# Human preview prints the exact `--confirm=<gb>` value; from JSON, sum actionable `findings[].size_bytes`, divide by 1073741824 (1 GiB), and truncate to an integer
devtrim trash-empty --only-devtrim
devtrim trash-empty --only-devtrim --json

# Only with explicit human authorization for permanent purge (`--confirm=<gb>` checks the new scan's truncated GiB total within ±2):
devtrim trash-empty --only-devtrim --confirm=<gb> --apply --yolo --json
```

### 5. Docker & local Buildx cache cleanup (permanent — bypasses Trash; never touches volumes)
```bash
devtrim clean docker --json
# Only with explicit human authorization (runs permanent `docker` prune commands; Docker selects eligible unused images/cache at execution):
devtrim clean docker --apply --yolo --json
```

### 6. Audit what was changed
```bash
devtrim history --limit 20 --json
```

## Command Reference

| Command | Mutates? | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `devtrim scan [--all] [--json]` | Read-only | All categories + largest findings (`--shred` previews permanent actions) |
| `devtrim disk [--warn-below SIZE] [--json]` | Read-only | Home volume free and total space (APFS snapshot count is shown in the TUI menu) |
| `devtrim explain <PATH> [--json]` | Read-only | Explains why a path is offered or protected |
| `devtrim worktrees [--root DIR] [--json]` | Read-only | Linked worktrees with size, `in-use`/`dirty`/`clean`, and UTC activity |
| `devtrim clean leftovers [--root DIR] [--json]` | Read-only | Ignored `.scratch`, abandoned `.git/objects/tmp_objdir-*`, `~/.ollama/models`, `~/.lmstudio/models` |
| `devtrim app-storage [--root DIR] [--json]` | Read-only | Metadata-only WhatsApp & Screen Studio inventory |
| `devtrim icloud [--json]` | Read-only | Large iCloud Drive files and local allocation |
| `devtrim largest [--top N] [--root DIR] [--json]` | Read-only | Largest directories under scan roots |
| `devtrim analyze [PATH] [--json]` | Read-only | Directory size breakdown (`--json` emits sizes without verdicts; use `explain` for JSON verdicts) |
| `devtrim dashboard [PATH] [--output FILE] [--no-open] [--json]` | Writes HTML | Writes a private offline HTML disk map and opens it unless `--no-open` is passed (`--json` also emits the snapshot JSON; pass `--no-open` in automation); never deletes targets |
| `devtrim status [--json]` | Read-only | Machine vitals and health score |
| `devtrim history [--limit N] [--json]` | Read-only | Write-ahead apply journal records |
| `devtrim purge [--root DIR] [--apply]` | Trash-first | Stale `node_modules` + corroborated build artifacts |
| `devtrim clean caches [--apply]` | Trash-first | Regenerable caches (HF, uv, npm, brew, cargo, bun, gh, pip, pnpm, CocoaPods, SwiftPM, Gradle, Go) |
| `devtrim clean node-modules [--root DIR] [--apply]` | Trash-first | Stale project `node_modules` |
| `devtrim clean artifacts [--root DIR] [--apply]` | Trash-first | Corroborated stale build directories (`target`, `.next`, `.turbo`, etc.) |
| `devtrim clean xcode [--apply]` | Trash-first | Idle `DerivedData` (preserving `SourcePackages`) & `DeviceSupport` |
| `devtrim clean docker [--apply]` | Permanent command | Unused local images, daemon build cache, and local `docker-container` Buildx builder caches (bypasses Trash; never volumes) |
| `devtrim clean simulators [--apply]` | Permanent command | Unavailable simulator devices by exact UDID (bypasses Trash) |
| `devtrim clean toolchains [--apply]` | Trash-first | Unreferenced `swift.org` toolchains |
| `devtrim clean installers [--apply]` | Trash-first | Stale `.dmg`/`.pkg` installers in Downloads/Desktop |
| `devtrim clean agents [--apply]` | Trash-first | Agent caches, superseded Codex releases, and stale session history |
| `devtrim optimize --task <NAME> [--apply]` | Command | macOS maintenance (`quicklook`, `fonts`, `launch-services`); `--apply` requires an explicit `--task` |
| `devtrim trash-empty [--only-devtrim] [--confirm=<gb>] [--apply]` | Permanent | Permanent Trash purge (`--confirm=<gb>` is required only when `--apply` has actionable items; `--only-devtrim` restricts to items journaled by devtrim) |

## JSON Envelopes (`--json`)

Cleanup and finding-list `--json` responses (`clean`, `purge`, `trash-empty`, `optimize`, `scan`, `worktrees`, `app-storage`, `icloud`, `largest`, `uninstall`, `analyze`) contain:
- `operation` (string): category or command name
- `applied` (bool): `false` on preview or pre-apply refusal, `true` once apply starts
- `findings` (array): `{ label, path, size_bytes, frees_at_least_bytes?, danger, action: { type, ... }, note, project? }`
- `results` (array, apply only, actionable findings only; `[]` on an empty successful apply; may still appear without `summary` if apply aborts with a fatal error): `{ finding, path?, status: "ok" | "error" | "not_attempted", error? }`
- `summary` (object, apply only; zero-valued on an empty successful apply, omitted on pre-apply refusal or fatal apply error): `{ op, items_touched, bytes_freed_estimate, bytes_trashed_estimate, home_volume?, notes }`, where `home_volume` (present whenever volume measurement ran around the apply) is `{ free_before, free_after, gained_bytes }` or `{ error }`
- `errors` (array of strings): non-empty causes nonzero exit status

Specialized read-only `--json` documents (on normal execution; CLI/flag refusals on these commands can still return the generic `{ operation, applied: false, findings: [], errors }` error envelope):
- `disk --json`: `{ operation, available_bytes, total_bytes, warn_below_bytes, below, errors }`
- `explain <PATH> --json`: `{ operation, path, protected: { builtin, config }, findings, errors }`
- `history --json`: `{ operation, entries, truncated, errors }`
- `dashboard --json`: offline dashboard inventory snapshot JSON
- `status --json`: system vitals snapshot object (including `unavailable` for probes that could not run; does not emit `operation` or `errors`)

## Default Project Scan Roots

Without `--root` or `~/.config/devtrim.toml` `roots = [...]`, project scans inspect only existing directories among:
`~/dev`, `~/Developer`, `~/Development`, `~/Projects`, `~/Code`, `~/GitHub`, `~/Repos`, `~/Workspace`, `~/www`, `~/.codex/worktrees`, `~/.t3/worktrees`.
